what: Amdocs makes the software that telecom companies use to run billing, customer care and network operations, and increasingly provides cloud migration and AI services to them.
customers: Large telecom operators such as AT&T, T-Mobile and Vodafone.
money: Long-term contracts to run telecom billing and operations systems.
moat: Its systems are deeply embedded in operators’ core processes, so switching is costly and rare, which produces long, recurring contracts.
risks: Revenue fell from $5.0B in 2024 to $4.5B in 2025 after exiting low-margin work.
Dependence on a few large customers, especially AT&T.
Fear that AI will replace parts of its services has hit the share price.
opportunities: At about 7–9 times earnings and a dividend yield near 5.5%, the shares are very cheap.
Free cash flow of about $560–700M a year.
Cloud and AI migration projects give telecoms reasons to spend.
watch: Revenue growth after the exit from low-margin work, and AI-related demand.
view: Amdocs has fallen to about 7 times forward earnings with a dividend yield near 5.5%, a price that implies the business is in structural decline. The fear is that AI will automate much of what its services teams do for telecom operators.

The business itself is steady: free cash flow of around $600 million a year, long contracts and systems that customers rarely replace. The revenue drop in 2025 came mainly from deliberately exiting low-margin work.

This turns on whether AI is a threat or an opportunity for Amdocs. I think its embedded position makes it more likely to sell AI tools to its customers than to be replaced, and at this price the shares look cheap.
bull: AI and cloud projects drive growth and the market re-rates a cash-rich software firm.
bear: AI shrinks the services market and revenue keeps falling.
